```plato
    //==
    // # PolygonWithHoles2D

    // The boundary's area less every hole's area.
    Area(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Number
        => r.Boundary.Area - SumOf(r.Holes.Map(h => h.Area));
```

```plato
    //==
    // # PolygonSet2D
    //
    // The components are mutually disjoint, so every measure is a plain sum and
    // containment is a disjunction.

    // The summed area of the components.
    Area(s: PolygonSet2D): Number
        => SumOf(s.Polygons.Map(p => p.Area));
```

```plato
    // n * R * r * sin(pi/n): the star is 2n triangles from the centre, each with
    // sides R and r meeting at pi/n, so each has area (1/2)*R*r*sin(pi/n).
    Area(s: RegularStar2D): Number
        => s.PointCount.ToNumber * s.OuterRadius * s.InnerRadius
        * (0.5 / s.PointCount.ToNumber).Turns.Sin;
```

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato, line 325](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato#L325).

```plato

    //==
    // # Planar-polygon-in-space, prism, and pyramid bodies
    //
    // Area, perimeter, centroid, normal, nearest-point, volume, surface-area, bounds and
    // containment bodies for the types declared in `polygons.types.plato`. They are
    // written in terms of the space kernels above.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here:
    //
    //   * Polygon3D is assumed PLANAR (its declaration says so) and SIMPLE.
    //   * CONTAINMENT in the plane is the even-odd rule projected into the polygon's own
    //     plane, so a point exactly on a boundary edge is not classified reliably. The
    //     prism's and pyramid's height parameters ARE boundary inclusive.
    //   * `Area` and `Volume` are NON-NEGATIVE.

    //==
    // # Polygon3D

    // The magnitude of the vector area (Newell). Exact for a planar ring; for a
    // non-planar ring it is the area of the ring's projection onto the best-fit
    // plane, which the declaration's planarity invariant rules out.
    Area(p: Polygon3D): Number
        => p.Points.VectorArea.Magnitude;
```
